title: What Kazzi's thinking adds to our workflow
summary: Kazzi showed how you think about picking up work. These are the ideas I'd fold into Review, on the Mac first and therefore on the phone too, not a port of Kazzi.

checks.text: The project is the unit, not the task. Kazzi's "you pick up a project" confirms Review's shape: the phone opens on projects, each showing whose move it is, and a project opens onto its cards.

Whose move is it? Each project shows one of three answers: yours (cards waiting), the agent's (working on…), or someone else's (a question out with Luke). It's a sharper line than a count, and it fits the agent states we already have.
The clock counts from your last move, not from the start, so it answers "is it my move again?" That suits a question out with someone, and a card that's been waiting on you.
Queue notes while the agent works. On the phone, "Send to agent" can hold notes and send them one at a time when the agent is free, rather than all at once mid-turn.
A note to yourself on the way out, shown with its age, next to the agent's "since you last looked".

What we don't take: Kazzi's collections, its models and its single-player rule. The agent writes to the board, so things do arrive overnight. Review's data contract (cards, answers, the Record) stays the one model.
